record.original_question: Let ABC be an isosceles triangle with AB = AC, let AD be the altitude from A, and let H be the orthocenter. For a point P on AD, project P orthogonally to AB and AC, and let P* be the point on AD where the two corresponding cevians from C and B intersect. Starting from P[0] = P and iterating P[n+1] = P[n]*, analyze the modes of convergence in cases not already covered by the monotone acute-triangle case with the starting point below A and outside the exceptional points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$, let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ onto $BC$, and let $H$ denote the orthocenter of $ABC$. For any point $P$ lying on the segment (or line) $AD$, define a new point $P^{\ast}$ on $AD$ by the following construction:

1. Let $P_b$ be the orthogonal projection of $P$ onto line $AB$, and let $P_c$ be the orthogonal projection of $P$ onto line $AC$.
2. Draw the cevian from $C$ through $P_b$ and the cevian from $B$ through $P_c$. By the symmetry of the configuration, these two cevians meet on the line $AD$; let $P^{\ast}$ be their intersection point.

Starting from an arbitrary point $P_0 = P$ on line $AD$, define the iteration $P_{n+1} = P_n^{\ast}$ for $n \geq 0$.

It is known that, when $ABC$ is acute and $P_0$ lies on the segment $AD$ strictly below $A$ and avoids a finite set of exceptional points, the sequence $\{P_n\}$ converges monotonically (to the orthocenter $H$).

Determine and classify the modes of convergence (or non-convergence) of the iteration $\{P_n\}_{n \ge 0}$ in all remaining cases, namely:
(a) when $ABC$ is right-angled or obtuse at $A$ (or at $B,C$),
(b) when the starting point $P_0$ lies on line $AD$ outside the segment from $A$ to $D$, and
(c) when $P_0$ coincides with or is near one of the exceptional points excluded from the known monotone case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open project for further investigation; the original framing explicitly notes that examining these convergence modes "may turn out to be a nice project." No published resolution was located.
